findings.text: Fixed UV hub MMR offsets observed: event-occurred alias, external IO interrupt broadcast, interrupt compare B, and IPI interrupt each have a single constant offset independent of hardware revision.

GR0 GAM GR configuration MMR offset depends on detected UV generation: newer generations share one smaller offset while older generations share a larger offset, with a zero fallback when no known generation matches.

GR0 and GR1 TLB interrupt configuration MMR offsets are selected by generation. GR0 pair uses the same offset across three older generations; GR1 pair uses a distinct offset on one generation versus the other two. Unsupported generations invoke an undefined-marker path rather than returning an address.

External IO interrupt broadcast register is modeled as a 64-bit value with interchangeable revision views. Every view exposes a single writable enable control at the least significant position and treats all remaining positions as reserved.

GR0 GAM GR configuration register is modeled as a 64-bit value with revision-specific views. Common and newer views expose only a writable subspace control in the low bits with surrounding reserved ranges; one older view adds a writable socket field in the lowest bits plus an undefined hole; the oldest view instead exposes a small writable group-count field at the bottom with the rest reserved.

Each TLB interrupt configuration register for both GR0 and GR1 and both interrupt indices shares an identical 64-bit layout across all revision views: a low interrupt vector selector, delivery mode and destination mode controls, status indicators, mask control, reserved gaps, and a wide APIC destination identifier in the upper half.

Interrupt compare B register is modeled as a 64-bit value with identical views across revisions: a wide writable real-time compare value occupying the lower majority of bits and a small reserved field at the top.

Tail of an event-occurred revision view contains a dense sequence of single-bit writable real-time clock indicators followed by a wide reserved upper region, indicating per-source event latching packed into one 64-bit word.

Small control fields use documented shift and single-bit or narrow masks: broadcast enable at bit zero, subspace control at bit ten, socket selector in the lowest six bits on one revision, group count in the lowest four bits on another, and compare value starting at bit zero with only the top byte excluded.

In TLB interrupt configuration words, vector, delivery mode, destination mode, mask, and APIC identifier are writable, while status and two delivery-state indicators are read-only; bit positions and widths are identical across GR0 versus GR1, interrupt 0 versus 1, and all revision views.

Address selection differs on unknown hardware: the GAM configuration macro can silently yield zero, risking access to the wrong MMR, whereas the TLB interrupt macros route through an explicit undefined marker, so callers must not assume a valid address without generation validation.

This header family exports the addressing and decoding interface for the covered UV MMRs: per-register offset selectors plus per-field shift and mask values and whole-word versus bitfield overlay types for use by hub drivers.
